tests.name: Quick Check
tests.description: Timed check on Movement Analysis in Sport

questions.question: Identify the joint, movement and agonist muscle when a cricketer bowls the ball forward.
questions.correctAnswer: Joint: Shoulder (ball-and-socket). Movement: Flexion (the arm swings forwards and upwards). Agonist: Anterior deltoids and pectorals.

questions.question: Describe the movement at the knee during the upward phase of a squat and name the agonist muscle.
questions.correctAnswer: Movement: Extension at the knee (the angle increases as the leg straightens). Agonist: Quadriceps contract concentrically.

questions.question: What movement occurs at the shoulder during the arm-raising phase of a star jump? Name the agonist muscle.
questions.correctAnswer: Movement: Abduction at the shoulder (the arms move away from the midline of the body). Agonist: Deltoids (middle fibres).

tests.name: Exam-Style Practice
tests.description: Short-answer practice on Movement Analysis in Sport

questions.question: Explain the difference between plantar flexion and dorsiflexion, giving a sporting example of each.
questions.correctAnswer: Plantar flexion is pointing the foot downward (e.g. rising onto toes in a sprint start, using the gastrocnemius). Dorsiflexion is pulling the foot upward towards the shin (e.g. lifting the foot when walking uphill, using the tibialis anterior).

questions.question: Describe the movement at the hip when a footballer kicks a ball and name the agonist and antagonist muscles.
questions.correctAnswer: Movement: Flexion at the hip (the leg swings forwards). Agonist: Iliopsoas (hip flexors). Antagonist: Gluteals (relax to allow the hip to flex).

questions.question: During a press-up, describe the movement at the elbow when pushing up and state the agonist muscle.
questions.correctAnswer: Movement: Extension at the elbow (the arm straightens). Agonist: Triceps contracts concentrically to push the body upwards.
